content.intro: This lesson covers agent frameworks and protocols through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Treat agentic systems as bounded loops over plans, state, tools, observations, and stopping conditions. Prefer deterministic workflows when they meet the need more reliably.
content.why_it_matters: Framework-independent agent design describes one part of a controlled action loop. The model may propose a step, but the application should independently validate the arguments, check the caller's permissions, enforce step/time limits, and record the actual tool result before deciding what happens next.

items.title: Model Context Protocol concepts
items.text: Treat model context protocol concepts as part of the model's input contract: state the task, provide only relevant context, specify what a good response looks like, and test representative and ambiguous cases. A prompt can guide behavior, but application code must still validate important outputs.

items.title: Protocol permissions and compatibility
items.text: Protocol permissions and compatibility is a control problem as much as a model-behavior problem. Establish explicit boundaries in trusted application code, minimize data exposure, test realistic misuse and failure cases, and record who is responsible for reviewing residual risk. A prompt alone is not a security boundary.

content.task: Practice framework-independent agent design within agent frameworks and protocols: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.
